regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 23" over the week, 20" of it on Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 23" to 38" from Friday through Sunday night. A Winter Storm Watch runs Friday through Monday. Palisades has 16" and Sugar Bowl 16".

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth gets 11", mostly Friday, with 10" expected. Southwest wind 20 to 25 mph with gusts to 65 mph Friday night. The NWS is calling for more, 9" to 17" from Friday through Sunday night. A Winter Storm Watch runs Friday through Saturday.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Whiteface leads with 10", 6" on Thursday. Killington also totals 10", 4" on Thursday, with light snow Friday. Jay Peak gets 7" with snow showers into the weekend. Expect cold, steady snow most of the period.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek leads with 9", all on Saturday, with snow showers likely and a slight chance of thunderstorms. Taos gets 4" Saturday and 1" Sunday. Expect cold, showery snow, with lows in the 20s.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Stevens Pass leads with 7", 6" on Sunday. Crystal Mountain totals 6", 5" of it Sunday. Mt. Baker gets 3" Sunday. Expect rain at lower elevations Friday and Saturday, with snow mixing in at the top.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler leads with 11", 9" on Sunday. Expect rain and showers Thursday through Saturday, with strong southeast wind Wednesday. Snow is mainly a Sunday story.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a Pacific system brings more rain and mountain snow to the West Coast around Monday Nov 16 into Tuesday Nov 17, with confidence in its own words only moderate.
